cue.zh-CN: 在可控行程内蹲起，脚掌稳定；不强求统一深度。

cue.en: Maintain trunk control; use the wall version if needed.

cue.zh-CN: 双脚着地抬髋，不用腰部过伸追求高度。
cue.en: Keep feet grounded; lift the hips without chasing height through lumbar extension.

cue.zh-CN: 缓慢交替移动对侧手脚，控制躯干。
cue.en: Move opposite arm and leg slowly while controlling the trunk.

cue.zh-CN: 四点支撑后小幅伸展对侧手脚，避免扭转。
cue.en: From all fours, reach opposite limbs without trunk rotation.

reviewStatus: editorial technique summary; coach review pending

cue.zh-CN: 分腿站稳，先做小行程，不急于负重。
cue.en: Set a stable split stance; begin with short range before adding load.

cue.zh-CN: 在平稳地面缓慢提踵，可轻扶稳定物体。

cue.zh-CN: 负重靠近胸前，保持脚掌支持，做可控行程。

cue.zh-CN: 髋向后移动，负重靠近腿；只到能控制的位置。

cue.zh-CN: 受控放低至上臂接近地面，安全拿起和放下负重。
cue.en: Lower under control until upper arms approach the floor; set weights down safely.

cue.zh-CN: 另一手轻撑自身大腿或稳定支撑，避免用躯干甩动。

cue.zh-CN: 仅使用可控、舒适的上推行程，避免明显后仰。
cue.en: Use a controlled, comfortable overhead range without excessive leaning.

cue.zh-CN: 先保证徒手版本稳定，再加轻负重。
cue.en: Establish control in the bodyweight version before adding light loads.

reviewStatus: editorial technique summary; coach review pending

cue.zh-CN: 肘部位置相对稳定，避免借助摆动。
cue.en: Keep elbow position fairly steady and avoid swinging.

reviewStatus: editorial technique summary; coach review pending

cue.zh-CN: 轻负重、可控抬起；不要耸肩猛甩。
cue.en: Use a light controlled lift rather than shrugging or jerking.

cue.en: Position the band around the upper back, not the neck; inspect it and secure the grip.

cue.en: Secure the band under both feet and hold it with hands, not around the neck.

cue.zh-CN: 双脚踩住带并握住两端，髋后移后站起。
cue.en: Stand on the band and hold it while hinging back and standing tall.

cue.zh-CN: 踩稳带，缓慢屈肘；不要放手弹回。
cue.en: Anchor securely underfoot and curl slowly; do not release into recoil.

cue.zh-CN: 调整座位和起始握位；先用轻负荷试行程。

cue.en: Adjust chest support, seat or foot supports. On a combo machine, select the low-row station and secure its handle. Pull without jerking backward.

cue.en: Adjust the seat and thigh restraint, then check a controllable range with a light load before pulling in front, not behind the neck. Follow the plate-loaded machine’s handles and arm paths rather than forcing a cable-bar trajectory.
